standard_prerequisites.name: Covering by affine etale neighbourhoods with normal domains of sections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma covering a point of a normal integral space by an affine etale neighbourhood whose ring of sections is a normal domain, and Properties, the lemma that the sections over such a neighbourhood form a normal domain
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, for every point, an affine etale neighbourhood U over which the relevant fraction is integral and the sections form a normal domain.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reducedness and generic points of etale neighbourhoods
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard properties of etale morphisms of schemes: the source is reduced and its generic points map to the generic point of the target, so a section that is a nonzerodivisor globally remains a nonzerodivisor after restriction
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the uniqueness of the solution of the equation b times f_U equals a over any etale neighbourhood.

core_obligations: Set up the integrality test (proof lines 544-552): let R be the ring of global functions, a domain; take an element f = a/b of its fraction field which is integral over R, and observe that for any etale neighbourhood U which is a scheme there is at most one element f_U of the sections over U with b f_U = a, because U is reduced and the restriction of b is a nonzerodivisor.

Solve locally (proof lines 552-558): for every point of the space choose an affine etale neighbourhood U as in the covering lemma; since the sections over U form a normal domain and f is integral over R, hence over those sections, the equation has a unique solution f_U over U.

Glue (proof lines 558-560): the uniqueness just observed shows that the local solutions agree on overlaps, so they glue to a global section of the structure sheaf, that is to an element of R; hence every integral element of the fraction field lies in R and R is normal.
proof_roadmap: Reduce normality to the statement that an integral element of the fraction field is global.
Use reducedness of etale neighbourhoods and the generic point condition for uniqueness of local solutions.
Solve locally by normality of the rings of sections on the covering and glue by uniqueness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the ring of global functions on a normal integral algebraic space is a normal domain (statement lines 538-542). The proof (proof lines 544-563) shows first that the ring is a domain, then reduces normality to the integrality of elements of the fraction field, solves the corresponding equation locally over affine etale neighbourhoods whose rings of sections are normal domains, and glues by a uniqueness argument based on reducedness. H2: a three-step argument with three inputs, written out in full.
